reconstructed_theorem_text: Let S be a compact second-countable topological space equipped with its Borel σ-algebra, Ω measurable with probability measure P, and X:ℝ₊×Ω→S jointly measurable. Let g:S→ℝ be continuous and A:ℝ₊×S→ℝ jointly measurable. Suppose for each T∈ℝ₊ that there exists a real C with |A(t,w)|≤C for all t≤T and w∈S. For each t∈ℝ₊ suppose there exists a P-integrable residual Z_t of zero mean such that g(X(t,ω))−g(X(0,ω))=∫_0^t A(v⁺,X(v⁺,ω))dv+Z_t(ω) for P-almost every ω, where v⁺=max(v,0). Let ρ_t=(X_t)_#P. Define F(r)=∫_S g dρ_{r⁺} and B(r)=∫_S A(r⁺,w)dρ_{r⁺}(w) for real r. Then B is locally Lebesgue-integrable on ℝ, F(b)−F(a)=∫_a^b B(v)dv for every a,b∈ℝ₊, F is absolutely continuous on every [0,T], T∈ℝ₊, and F′(t)=B(t) for Lebesgue-almost every t∈(0,∞).
objects: Measurable sample Ω, probability P, compact second-countable Borel state S, state process X, observable g, measurable generator A, centered residual witnesses Z, marginal law family ρ, and functions F and B.
domains: X and A have nonnegative time. F and B are defined on all ℝ with t.toNNReal=max(t,0). Both balance integrals are real interval integrals. The derivative measure is real Lebesgue volume restricted to Set.Ioi 0.
quantifiers: Each T has a single bound for all t≤T and states. For each t choose an integrable mean-zero Z and then assume the balance for P-a.e. ω. The endpoint identity is for every pair a,b∈ℝ₊, absolute continuity is for every T∈ℝ₊, and the derivative claim is a.e. for positive times.
assumptions: Joint measurability of X and A, continuity of g, the stated finite-horizon local bound, and the fixed-time centered balance. No sample-path continuity, filtration or martingale hypothesis is stated.
conclusion: Local integrability of B on the full real line, the signed integral identity on nonnegative endpoints, absolute continuity on each [0,T], and the ordinary derivative HasDerivAt F (B(t)) t for Lebesgue-a.e. positive t.
scopes: The explicit map sends P through X_t, with slice measurability witnessed by composing joint measurability with ω↦(t,ω), then passing to a.e. measurability. The interval integral is oriented: it uses the usual order when the lower endpoint is at most the upper endpoint, changes sign on reversing endpoints, and vanishes when the endpoints coincide. The absolute-continuity definition uses vanishing total interval length for finite disjoint intervals within [0,T]. The derivative is ordinary and restricted in its a.e. quantifier to positive real times. No derivative assertion at zero is present. Measure integrals use Lean's totalized Bochner convention.
constant_dependencies: Each horizon has its own bound C on A. The residual is centered with coefficient one and contributes no term to the law balance.
